answer: Score identity by the diversity of who attests to it, not by how many. A cluster that only vouches internally yields near-zero diversity and therefore near-zero weight. An attacker must recruit genuinely independent established peers to gain influence, at which point the accounts are no longer anonymous throwaway sybils but known, accountable participants. Concretely, this is the basalt rule: the ledger is the echo every attestation is measured against, and any unsupported claim is treated as island, not evidence.
